tax.text: Meeks opposed the Republican reconciliation law, condemning its cuts to health care and food assistance made to fund tax breaks for the wealthy.
tax.quote: Republicans failed the American people by passing their Big, Ugly Bill that delivers the largest cuts to health care and food assistance in American history.

wages.text: Meeks says he backs workers' right to organize and calls unions the backbone of the middle class.
wages.quote: All workers deserve the right to unionize and collectively bargain.

trade.text: Meeks has long supported free trade agreements, arguing greater market access boosts U.S. exports and jobs.
trade.quote: Greater access means more exports of U.S. goods and services, and that means more jobs for American workers.

debt.text: Meeks said the country must protect seniors' and veterans' benefits rather than strip them away.
debt.quote: We believe that it is our country's responsibility to serve our veterans, seniors, and taxpayers by working to protect their benefits and not stripping them away.

housing.text: Meeks backed a housing bill aimed at increasing supply by reducing barriers to construction.
housing.quote: enacting comprehensive reforms at the federal, state, and local levels aimed at reducing barriers to housing construction and increasing supply

safety.text: Meeks says he supports investing in community-based violence intervention programs.
safety.quote: investing in community-based violence intervention programs that are proven to save lives.

immigration.text: Meeks supports comprehensive immigration reform with a path to citizenship for Dreamers, TPS holders, and essential workers.
immigration.quote: I support comprehensive immigration reform that includes a path to citizenship for Dreamers, Temporary Protected Status (TPS) holders, farmworkers, and essential workers

guns.text: Meeks says he has consistently backed universal background checks and bans on assault weapons and high-capacity magazines.
guns.quote: I have consistently supported legislation that works towards implementing universal background checks, banning assault weapons and high-capacity magazines, closing loopholes, and investing in community-based violence intervention programs that are proven to save lives.

abortion.text: Meeks condemned the Supreme Court's decision overturning Roe v. Wade as stripping away women's rights.
abortion.quote: Today is a heartbreaking day where women across America had the rights over their own bodies stripped away by the stroke of a pen.

health.text: Meeks calls health care a right and pledges to protect the ACA, Medicare, and Medicaid.
health.quote: protecting access to the Affordable Care Act, to Medicare, and Medicaid–as well as supporting our local community health centers and hospital systems

energy.text: Meeks has called for urgent climate action and touts a clean energy economy.
energy.quote: A clean energy economy will create tens of thousands of good, high paying American jobs.

tax.text: Marsh's platform calls for lower taxes and a pro-growth tax policy with less regulation to grow private-sector jobs.
tax.quote:
Lower taxes, grow private jobs

Pro-growth tax policy, less red tape, energy abundance.

schools.text: Marsh's education platform emphasizes parents' rights, curriculum transparency, and school choice.
schools.quote:
Parents' rights & results

Curriculum transparency, choice, academics over ideology.

immigration.text: Marsh calls for securing the border through strong enforcement, ending catch-and-release, and interior removals.
immigration.quote:
Secure the border

Strong enforcement, end catch-and-release, interior removals.

guns.text: Marsh says he will defend gun rights and opposes new federal gun bans and registries.
guns.quote:
Defend gun rights

Opposes new federal gun bans and registries.

energy.text: Marsh backs an all-of-the-above, pro-production energy approach favoring oil, gas, and nuclear reliability over what he calls rushed mandates.
energy.quote:
All-of-the-above, pro-production

Oil, gas, nuclear, and reliability over rushed mandates.
